Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:66547
Court No. - 85
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 1591 of 2024

Appellant :- Sunil Yadav
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Appellant :- Vinay Kumar Singh
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention
of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection
order dated 11.1.2024 passed by the Special Judge (Sc/St Act), Gorakhpur.
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned AGA and perused the entire record.

However, despite service of notice, none is present for the opposite party no.2.
3.

The prosecution story, as unfolded in the F.I.R., is that the victim, the daughter of the informant,
was eve-teased by the appellant and subsequently he forcibly took away the victim from her house and without her consent committed rape with her and an obscene video was made viral on social media on the basis of which he started blackmailing the victim.
F.I.R. was lodged and after investigation now charge sheet has been submitted.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has not committed the present offence.

Alleged offences are Sunil Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196993238/
1 not attracted against him.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that there are material contradictions in the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC.

It is further submitted that from the perusal of the aforesaid statements it is explicitly clear that it was a case of consent and the victim was in touch of the accused appellant for a period of two years and they were in love affair with each other.
It is also submitted that the medical evidence does not corroborate the prosecution version.

Though the prosecution claims to have collected the evidence of obscene video pertaining to the victim but as a matter of fact there is no evidence under Section 67 I.T. Act and the I.O. has failed to collect any evidence to the effect that obscene / nude video of the prosecutrix was made viral on social media.
Prosecutrix is a major lady.
The Court concerned while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
Appellant is in jail since 22.9.2023.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.
5. On the other hand, learned AGA opposing the prayer for bail submitted that the appellant committed the present offence having knowledge that the victim belonged to scheduled caste community.

There is no infirmity or illegality in the impugned order but however he could not dispute this aspect of the matter that CDR has been collected by the I.O. regarding the conversation between prosecutrix and the appellant but no evidence under Section 67 I.T. Act has been collected by the I.O..
6. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

7. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The Court concerned erred in rejecting the bail application of the appellant.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is liable to be allowed.
8. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

9. Let the appellant Sunil Yadav involved in Case Crime No. 133 of 2023, under Sections 506, 376 IPC, 67 I.T. Act and 3(2) 5 SC/ST Act, P.S. Belipar, District Gorakhpur be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i). The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
